# Robot docs

A home-printable, fishing-line tendon humanoid, so far entirely in simulation. The design and the repository map are in the [README](https://github.com/displague/robot#readme). Each doc below is an experiment or a design note; its "Not yet" and "Next" sections are the backlog.

<!-- generated by tools/docs_index.py from each doc's front matter; edit the docs, not this file -->

Walking with a bag in hand is the open failure |
| [39 - Walking with a bag in hand: the balance loop must know the bag, and the grip must damp it (P-064, D-063)](39-walking-with-a-bag.md) | Why walking with a gripped bag failed: the balance loop did not know the bag, not the swing. A damped grip plus the felt weight walks 0.8 to 2.3 kg; with the bag set down before a sit (D-065), the chain grid goes from 10 to 17 or 18 of 24. One hand walks about 2.5 kg, two about 4.5 kg split (D-063) |

Its pitch now runs on two strands (D-066). The spine's overload traced to the rise's fast hip extension; pacing it at 22.5 deg/s (D-067) stands every chair case with no slip and less energy |

| [32 - The 8 m/s wind and getting up from a half-kneel (P-052, D-053)](32-wind-and-getup.md) | The 8 m/s wind (not the drag, the action range or the ankle drive mode: the policies lack the balance loop's ankle strategy) and getting up: no slow rise below a pelvis height of 0.90 m; a learned lunge rises from a half-kneel 61 % of the time (D-053) |
| [42 - Senses: sight, hearing, balance, and why people sway (P-066, research)](42-senses.md) | Research topic: the robot senses only its body (joints, lines, a pelvis IMU, foot loads), with no sight or sound. How eyes, ears and the inner ear split and fuse their inputs, why separate receptors evolved, and why people control loosely. A proposal for head stereo depth, binaural hearing, a head IMU, and a relaxed-control test |
| [43 - The next training rounds: senses, loose control, the nurturing helper, then a crew (P-067, D-069)](43-training-rounds.md) | The plan the owner queued: four training rounds that bring in the senses of docs/42, relaxed control, and a give-and-take helper faded to withdrawal, then the role flip, shelter tests and robots helping each other up. Overloading a line through the helper fails the episode, and withdrawal needs both a small helper impulse and the old gates passing (D-069) |
| [44 - The nurturing helper v0 on the 0.35 m chair (P-068, D-070)](44-helper-chair.md) | A scripted helper holds the robot's wrists and pulls along its arms in proportion to how far the CoM is behind the feet. With it the 0.35 m chair rise stands for the first time, with no learning. A firm helper overloads the elbows (2.35x their rating, against 1.42x unassisted) and fails D-069's first law; a yielding one passes. One hand, or a lopsided helper, is not enough, and with the helper withdrawn the rise fails as before |
| [45 - The drunken sailor, and training the chair rise with the helper as curriculum (P-069, P-070, D-071, D-072)](45-rise-training.md) | A wandering helper strains the elbows: 4 N of wander breaks the overload law with the firmer helper, and 8 N fails the rise through wrist-clutch slip. A cross-entropy search over the hand-written rise's 11 parameters, on the full model, faded the helper to a 1 N pull and then found a 0.35 m rise with no helper. A control with no helper at any point found a better one sooner: 0.35 to 0.45 m stand unassisted, 0.50 m is lost. So in this search the 0.35 m failure was tuning, and the helper's curriculum did not help. Those first rises were marginal under 2% parameter jitter. Retrained with the jitter and every seat in the score, the low-seat set stands on 0.35 m 23 of 24 times. It is now the default below 0.42 m (D-072), so the whole chair grid stands, and the gauntlet is unchanged |
